definitions.explanation: The act of breathing in deeply and slowly. Often done to calm nerves, relax, or take in fresh air.

examples.japanese: {深呼吸|しんこきゅう}をしてください。
{緊張|きんちょう}したときは{深呼吸|しんこきゅう}すると{落|お}ち{着|つ}く。
examples.english: Taking deep breaths when nervous helps you calm down.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{新鮮|しんせん}な{空気|くうき}を{吸|す}いながら{深呼吸|しんこきゅう}した。
examples.english: I took deep breaths while breathing in the fresh morning air.

notes:
{深呼吸|しんこきゅう} means breathing in deeply and slowly. A compound of {深|しん} (deep) + {呼吸|こきゅう} (breathing). Used with する as a verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深呼吸|しんこきゅう}（を）する (to take a deep breath)
- {大|おお}きく{深呼吸|しんこきゅう}する (to take a big deep breath)
- {深呼吸|しんこきゅう}して{落|お}ち{着|つ}く (to calm down by breathing deeply)
- {深呼吸|しんこきゅう}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す (to take repeated deep breaths)

USAGE:
Commonly recommended as a way to calm nerves ({緊張|きんちょう}をほぐす), relieve stress, or enjoy fresh air. Often heard in medical, exercise, and relaxation contexts. Both {深呼吸|しんこきゅう}する and {深呼吸|しんこきゅう}をする are natural.

RELATED WORDS:
- {呼吸|こきゅう}: breathing (general)
- {腹式|ふくしき}{呼吸|こきゅう}: abdominal/diaphragmatic breathing
- {息|いき}を{吸|す}う: to inhale
- {息|いき}を{吐|は}く: to exhale
